ai.description: This viper reaches 70–90 cm. It is brown with dark, pale-centered lateral blotches and a distinct postocular stripe. Key features include a triangular head and a heat-sensing loreal pit.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Protobothrops himalayanus* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged, reddish-brown dorsal blotches that fuse into a continuous zigzag stripe along the mid-dorsum.
ai.habitat: *Protobothrops himalayanus* inhabits moist, dense broadleaf and coniferous forests within the Himalayan foothills at elevations typically ranging from 1,500 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Protobothrops himalayanus* is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless for long periods to ambush small mammals and amphibians under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Protobothrops himalayanus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–10 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Protobothrops himalayanus* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim at elevations between 1,500–3,000m.
